reason: The key premises are directly and accurately supported by the cited evidence (E3, E4, E5), which reports the same UHPS conditions, quantitative property improvements, microstructural features, and oxidation behavior. The conflicting evidence (E1, E2) discusses liquid-phase sintering with additives and does not contradict the premises about single-phase UHPS ZrB2.
premises: UHPS at 15 GPa and 1450 °C yields fully dense, grain-refined ZrB2 with high dislocation density
UHPS-processed ZrB2 exhibits ~46% higher hardness and ~69% higher fracture toughness than high-temperature sintered ZrB2
UHPS-processed ZrB2 shows an oxidation threshold increase of ~250 °C relative to high-temperature sintered ZrB2
The refined grain size and high dislocation density enhance mechanical properties via Hall–Petch and Taylor strengthening
The nanostructured surface layers densify upon oxidation to form a protective ZrO2 barrier
